name: TryRapVideo
tagline: Make short rap videos from a photo, an idea, or original English lyrics.

pricing.basis: monthly subscription with 300 credits per month
pricing.notes: The number of videos per month varies with clip length and resolution.
pricing.freeTier: Eligible new users can receive welcome credits after email verification.

verdictSummary: A personal rap greeting with a photo, original lyrics, and a beat is feasible in a weekend. Matching the hosted workflow's generated motion and timing requires a model or API and substantial testing across different photos and voices.
coreLoopDIY: Render a downloadable rap greeting from a photo, a short recording, and a beat with timed captions.
diyTimeEstimate: one weekend for a local prototype
requirements: A photo and audio the user has permission to use
moatNotes: The polished part is getting from a photo and a prompt to a coherent, shareable clip with minimal manual timing.
whyPeopleStillPay: The service handles generation, timing, and rendering in one workflow, which saves the manual audio and video editing a simple local prototype needs.
notes: Proposed by the maker. The prompt builds a personal rap greeting with user-supplied audio.
prompt:
Build a local rap greeting maker in an empty folder.
Use Python 3.12, Flask, and a locally installed FFmpeg with libass.
Serve the UI on 127.0.0.1 and keep all media on the machine.
Accept one JPG or PNG photo, a short vocal recording, and an optional beat the user has permission to use.
Accept original English lyrics as SRT text for timed captions.
Validate supported file types and cap total uploads at 25 MB.
Use ffprobe to reject unreadable media and vocal clips longer than 15 seconds.
Offer 9:16 and 1:1 output at 720p.
Scale the photo to fit without cropping, with black padding.
Loop the beat if needed, reduce its volume, and trim the mix to the vocal length.
Burn captions with libass and render an H.264 MP4 with AAC audio.
Use a unique temporary directory per render and pass FFmpeg arguments as a list.
Show an actionable error if FFmpeg is missing or the render fails.
Show a local preview and a download link for the rendered MP4.
Keep output in the temp directory and clean it up after the download finishes.
Leave out accounts, billing, voice cloning, and generated lip sync.
Write a README with installation, launch instructions, and an example SRT file.
